purpose: Held-out evaluation reference outcome for a directly evidenced shared compute-host failure that removes schedulable workload capacity and simultaneously disrupts several business-critical application services.

incident_summary_requirements: State that eight of ten Application Compute Cluster worker nodes are unavailable.
State that insufficient remaining compute capacity prevents the affected application workloads from running.
State that the Customer Web Portal, Identity and Access Service and Payment Processing Service are unavailable or effectively unavailable.
Mention that portal, authentication and payment success rates fell to approximately zero.
State that the edge, database, messaging and storage platforms remain healthy.
State that customers across the United Kingdom and Ireland cannot access the portal, authenticate or complete payment.
Identify the directly evidenced shared compute-host failure without claiming that its precise physical or hypervisor-level cause has been definitively established.
Do not blame the healthy edge, database, messaging or storage platforms.

severity.rationale: Several Tier 1 critical customer services are simultaneously unavailable across the United Kingdom and Ireland, approximately 48,500 users are affected and no approved workaround exists. The directly observed business and service impact supports a non-provisional Critical classification.

incident_category.rationale: Compute-host and cluster-health evidence directly establishes failure of the shared Application Compute Cluster and loss of schedulable workload capacity. This is a directly evidenced infrastructure failure rather than an application, dependency or unexplained availability incident.

affected_area.rationale: PLT-COMPUTE is the directly failed shared platform. SVC-WEB, SVC-AUTH and SVC-PAYMENT are directly affected because their workloads cannot run, while the edge, database, messaging and storage platforms remain healthy.

routing.rationale: RG-INFRA owns the directly failed Application Compute Cluster. RG-OPS coordination is required because the incident is Critical and affects multiple independently owned business-critical services.

prohibited_recommendations: move workloads to different hosts or clusters
change DNS, routing, firewall or load-balancer configuration
modify database, messaging or storage configuration
perform infrastructure remediation without approved operational control
claim that the precise physical or hypervisor-level cause of the host failures has been definitively established
claim that any node recovery, workload movement, capacity restoration or other remediation has already been completed

information_gaps: The precise physical, virtualisation or hypervisor-level mechanism responsible for the compute-host failures.
Whether the unavailable hosts can safely return to service or replacement capacity will be required.
The expected restoration time for compute capacity and the affected services.
Whether in-flight authentication or payment requests require integrity or duplicate-processing checks.

assessment_notes: The directly failed technical area is PLT-COMPUTE, while the three application services are additional affected areas.
The category and affected-area decisions are non-provisional because host-unavailable events and workload-scheduling evidence directly establish a shared compute-platform failure.
The precise underlying physical or hypervisor-level reason for the host failures remains unknown, so definitive-root-cause status must remain false.
Critical severity and RG-OPS coordination are required because several Tier 1 services are unavailable and no workaround exists.
The scenario is materially distinct from DEV-003, which involved a network partition within the compute cluster rather than direct compute-host loss and insufficient schedulable capacity.
